---
title: "Cross-Validation for Genomic Prediction Models"
---

## Cross-Validation for Genomic Prediction Models {.unnumbered}


### Description

Performs k-fold or leave-one-out (LOO) cross-validation to estimate
prediction accuracy of genomic models fitted with <code>masreml()</code>.
Individuals are split into training and validation sets; the model
is trained on each training set and used to predict the held-out
validation individuals.



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>cv_masreml(
  y,
  X = NULL,
  markers = NULL,
  G = NULL,
  folds = 5L,
  scheme = "random",
  method = "auto",
  solver = "auto",
  max_iter = 100L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  n_threads = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="y">y</code></td>
<td>
numeric vector of phenotypes (length n)
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="X">X</code></td>
<td>
fixed effects matrix (n x c). NULL = intercept only
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="markers">markers</code></td>
<td>
list of raw marker inputs (see <code>masreml</code>)
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="G">G</code></td>
<td>
list of pre-built G matrices (see <code>masreml</code>)
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="folds">folds</code></td>
<td>
integer, number of CV folds (default 5).
Use <code>folds = length(y)</code> for leave-one-out (LOO).
Larger values give less biased but more variable estimates.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="scheme">scheme</code></td>
<td>
character, fold assignment scheme:


<ul>
<li> <code>"random"</code> (default): individuals randomly assigned
to folds — recommended for most cases

</li>
<li> <code>"systematic"</code>: every k-th individual assigned to
same fold — useful for structured populations

</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="method">method</code></td>
<td>
character, REML method (see <code>masreml</code>)
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="solver">solver</code></td>
<td>
character, EBV solver (see <code>masreml</code>)
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="max_iter">max_iter</code></td>
<td>
integer, max REML iterations
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="tol">tol</code></td>
<td>
numeric, convergence tolerance
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="n_threads">n_threads</code></td>
<td>
integer, number of threads
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="seed">seed</code></td>
<td>
integer, random seed for reproducibility
</td></tr>
</table>


### Value

Object of class <code>"masreml_cv"</code> with elements:


<ul>
<li> <code>accuracy</code>: mean prediction accuracy (r_MG)

</li>
<li> <code>accuracy_fold</code>: accuracy per fold

</li>
<li> <code>bias</code>: mean regression slope (bias check)

</li>
<li> <code>bias_fold</code>: slope per fold

</li>
<li> <code>gebv_all</code>: GEBV for all individuals

</li>
<li> <code>fold_assignments</code>: fold ID per individual

</li>
<li> <code>folds</code>: number of folds used

</li>
<li> <code>scheme</code>: fold scheme used

</li>
<li> <code>call</code>: matched call

</li></ul>



### See Also

<code>masreml</code>, <code>compute_accuracy</code>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masreml")

# 5-fold cross-validation
cv <- cv_masreml(
  y       = y,
  markers = list(snp_add = W),
  folds   = 5,
  seed    = 42
)
summary(cv)

# Leave-one-out cross-validation
cv_loo <- cv_masreml(
  y     = y,
  markers = list(snp_add = W),
  folds = length(y)
)
summary(cv_loo)




```
